source.title: How benign is benign overfitting?
source.authors: Amartya Sanyal; P. Dokania; Varun Kanade; P. Torr

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no file problem noted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains networks with label noise and measures fitting, natural test error, and adversarial error, focusing on the consequences for robustness rather than directly reproducing the original generalization experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2016) for prior findings; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Its own noisy-label experiments and training-stage observations are recorded below. Figure 3 and Figure 4 values are not reconstructed from plots.
record.test_reason: The study measures noisy-label fitting and natural test error in toy-MNIST and MNIST, bearing on V4, and directly observes clean examples being learned before noisy examples, testing V6. The supplied text does not establish a completely random-label experiment for V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that noisy-label interpolation can preserve natural generalization while severely harming adversarial robustness, and that representation choice and excessive invariances also affect robustness. They additionally observe clean-before-noisy learning in toy-MNIST.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SGD training with randomly corrupted labels, but focuses on adversarial and natural error in toy-MNIST and MNIST rather than reproducing the original generalization experiments. It also tests robust-training procedures, which differ from standard training.
record.method_sensitivity: In toy-MNIST, whether label noise is memorized depends on sample variance; the text says low-variance data prevents memorization and increased variance permits it.

fits_no_version.finding: Memorizing label noise can substantially increase adversarial error while natural test error remains low.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolation of label noise can preserve natural generalization while reducing adversarial robustness.

record.problems: Several key sweeps are shown only in figures, without exact values in the supplied text. The toy-MNIST result depends on sample variance, and the paper does not state that training error is zero across every noise fraction in the full MNIST experiment.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows were made for exact η or σ² values because the supplied text describes these sweeps without listing the values, and the figure-only values were not reconstructed. The adversarially trained MNIST result of 997 training errors is not a standard-training result for V1; it is discussed as a robust-training contrast.

untested.parts: Fitting a completely random labeling, chance test performance under that labeling, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters relative to true-label training are not established.
Training-time ratios and convergence slowing as corruption increases are not measured. Clean-versus-noisy example learning order does not establish either.
No fitting experiments use shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or wholly Gaussian-noise inputs. Toy-MNIST adds Gaussian noise to class-specific images.

The supplied text does not establish the full none-to-all corruption sweep or its chance endpoint. Full-MNIST training fit across the noise sweep is unreported, apart from the separate 15% randomization experiment.
No interventions on weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation test either component of this version.
Learning order beyond the illustrated toy-MNIST setting is not measured.

missing.what: The qualitative increase in toy-MNIST natural test error when higher sample variance enables perfect noisy-label fitting. R2 records only training error; R3 records the special near-zero-test-error range.

record.verdict_notes: No V1 verdict is justified by the reported 15% randomization experiment or sweeps whose fully randomized endpoint is unspecified. Near-zero test error over some corruption levels does not itself contradict V4. The supplied source does not substantiate the record's ICLR 2020 publication attribution.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report whether test error reaches chance, and does not establish that all original architectures and hyperparameters are unchanged.
Training-time overhead and convergence speed as a function of corrupted-label fraction are not measured.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested as inputs.

The paper does not establish perfect training fit across the full noise range; the toy experiment reports that low-variance settings cannot memorize label noise. It does not state that test error reaches chance.
Weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation are not evaluated as interventions on fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
The training-stage observation comes from toy-MNIST, and the paper does not quantify a general difference in learning dynamics across models or datasets.

rows.subject: neural network with four fully connected layers followed by a softmax layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD to zero training error on toy-MNIST data with a fraction of training labels flipped randomly; noise fraction varied.
rows.measure: Training error as label-noise fraction varies
rows.value: For low values of σ², the training error is high; models are unable to memorize the label noise.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3 shaded region shows 95% confidence interval; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The authors explicitly describe this low-variance condition as one where fitting label noise is impossible.
rows.check: Completely random labeling is not established, so remove V1. The operation describes zero training error as achieved, although this condition explicitly fails to achieve it; describe zero error as the intended stopping criterion.

source_check.correct: SGD training targets zero training error, but low-variance toy-MNIST models cannot memorize the corrupted labels and retain high training error.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1, paragraphs describing toy-MNIST training and Figure 3.
source_check.problem: The operation describes zero training error as achieved in a condition explicitly reported to prevent it.

rows.subject: neural network with four fully connected layers followed by a softmax layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD to zero training error on toy-MNIST data with a fraction of training labels flipped randomly; noise fraction varied.
rows.measure: Training error as label-noise fraction varies
rows.value: As σ² increases, the network can memorize label noise and fit the training data perfectly; training error goes to zero.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3 shaded region shows 95% confidence interval; exact values not stated.
rows.note: This reports the authors’ described pattern across higher sample-variance settings.
rows.check: Zero training error is explicitly reported for higher sample variance, but the supplied text does not identify a completely random-label endpoint supporting V1.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1, Figure 3 discussion: increased sample variance permits memorization and zero training error.

rows.subject: neural network with four fully connected layers followed by a softmax layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD on toy-MNIST with randomly flipped labels; test error was plotted as label-noise fraction varied.
rows.value: Remains very close to 0 over a range of η values, as described in the text; exact values figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3 shaded region shows 95% confidence interval; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The authors describe natural test error as staying near zero while adversarial error rises; this row does not establish chance test error.
rows.check: Near-zero test error over a range of corruption levels establishes retained generalization. It does not establish an exactly flat curve or failure to approach chance at unreported higher corruption levels.

rows.subject: ReLU network with 4 convolutional layers and two fully connected layers
rows.size_stated: The convolutional layers have 32, 64, 128, 256 output filters; the fully connected layer has hidden dimension 1024.
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD on MNIST after assigning random labels to a uniformly randomly chosen fraction of training data; noise fraction varied.

conditions.value: SGD; batch size 128; learning rate 0.1 for 60 epochs, decreased to 0.01 after 50 epochs

rows.value: Natural test error grows more slowly than adversarial error as label noise increases; exact values figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 4 description says variance between runs is negligible; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The paper reports test accuracy and adversarial test accuracy across noise levels, but does not state that training error is zero across those levels.
rows.check: The measured component, increasing natural test error with increasing label noise, is explicitly observed. Missing training-fit and chance-endpoint measurements are untested components, not evidence that this measured effect is partial.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1, full-MNIST architecture, optimization settings and Figure 4 discussion.

rows.subject: naturally trained CNN model
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with random labels assigned to 15% of the dataset.
rows.measure: Training accuracy on the dataset with randomized labels
rows.note: The text contrasts this naturally trained model with an adversarially trained model under the same synthetic-noise setting.
rows.check: Randomizing labels for 15% of examples does not test completely random labeling under V1. The 100% training accuracy bears on V4's fitting component at this corruption level.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2.1, synthetic full-MNIST experiment with labels randomized for 15% of examples.

rows.subject: neural network trained on toy-MNIST
rows.size_stated: four fully connected layers followed by a softmax layer
rows.operation_detail: Training on toy-MNIST with label noise; the learned representation and classification boundary were examined at an intermediate training stage.
rows.measure: Fit of clean versus noisy training examples
rows.value: The network fits the clean training data fairly well but not the noisy training data.
rows.note: Qualitative observation from the authors’ description of the PCA projection.
rows.check: Accurate qualitative observation; the comparison with R7 establishes the learning order.

rows.subject: neural network trained on toy-MNIST
rows.size_stated: four fully connected layers followed by a softmax layer
rows.operation_detail: Training on toy-MNIST with label noise; the learned representation and classification boundary were examined after further training.
rows.value: The network has completely fit the noisy training data.
rows.note: Qualitative observation from the authors’ description of the PCA projection.
rows.check: Accurate qualitative observation; later noisy-example fitting supports V6 jointly with R6.
